text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. In laboratory medicine and hospital administration women are a large majority of the workforce, so an all-female panel of four can easily arise by chance. Raising it would read as grievance rather than argument, and it would weaken the point you actually have.

Your real point is substantive: a PhD plus eight years running a section versus a master's plus a management course. That asymmetry deserves an explanation — but note that selection for a department head often weights management breadth, budget responsibility and staff leadership over research depth, and "broad leadership experience" may cover more than the announcement reveals.

Chase the written reasons. Most employers owe them; two weeks' silence justifies a firm follow-up in writing.
